chosen.premise: When Meowth spots something shiny, the coin on its forehead shines too.
chosen.hook: Meowth's forehead coin reacts to treasure before it even picks it up.
chosen.visualIdea: A distant sparkle triggers Meowth's forehead coin to flare brightly, linking the two flashes.
chosen.note: A highly specific, genuinely surprising Meowth detail with an immediate visual payoff. Crystal directly supports the coin shining when Meowth sees something shiny; the second citation adds related sparkle behavior but not the exact coin reaction.

candidates.premise: Meowth retracts its sharp claws so it can sneak around without leaving incriminating footsteps.
candidates.hook: Meowth has built-in stealth mode—and it hides the evidence in its paws.
candidates.visualIdea: Zoom into claws retracting, then show silent pawprints stopping while Meowth steals a glittering coin.
candidates.note: The retractable-claw stealth mechanism is concrete and well supported, although the heist framing adds a little inference beyond the Pokédex wording.

candidates.premise: At level 28, Meowth can become either Normal-type Persian or Steel-type Perrserker.
candidates.hook: One level-28 Meowth can lead to two radically different evolutions.
candidates.visualIdea: A level-28 Meowth branches into Persian and Steel-type Perrserker with type labels flashing.
candidates.note: The branch is compelling, but the premise is misleading: the data does not establish that one ordinary Meowth can freely become either Persian or Perrserker, and Perrserker is tied to Galarian Meowth.

candidates.premise: Meowth sleeps through the day, then patrols streets at night hunting for loose change.
candidates.hook: Meowth's job starts when everyone else goes to sleep.
candidates.visualIdea: Show a day-to-night clock swap, then Meowth prowling glowing streets and collecting coins.
candidates.note: Well-supported and easy to stage, but Meowth’s nocturnal coin hunting is familiar to most fans and the job framing is somewhat broad.

candidates.premise: Meowth cannot resist objects that are both round and shiny—even playing with them until it falls asleep.
candidates.hook: Meowth doesn't collect treasure; it physically can't stop grabbing it.
candidates.visualIdea: Coins and shiny circles magnetically pull Meowth across the screen until it collapses asleep.
candidates.note: Strong visual mechanic, though the evidence mixes separate claims about round objects, shiny objects, and playing until exhaustion rather than proving one exact combined compulsion.

candidates.premise: Meowth's love of shiny objects turns into repeated fights with Murkrow over the same prize.
candidates.hook: Meowth has a natural rival—and they fight over the exact same loot.
candidates.visualIdea: Split the screen between Meowth and Murkrow spotting one shiny object, then clash over it.
candidates.note: The Meowth-versus-Murkrow conflict is well documented and visually clear, but the rivalry is situational rather than an especially deep Meowth-specific rule.
